# Review finding: client hard-requires a new protocol field before the provider ships it (P0, enhanced-settings task 1)

Pattern: when client and provider release independently, a client increment unconditionally sends a new request field (`require_receipt`) and rejects responses that lack a new response field (`applied is True`), even on the default path (enhanced_settings=False). Against the released provider (Git tag eval-release), which has no receipt support, every ordinary save then raises after the provider has already applied the values. That is a false failure, and it breaks the "independently releasable main" contract.

Detection: look for new response-field checks (`response.get(new_field) is not True`) that are not gated by a feature flag or capability negotiation, and for tests whose fake provider returns only the new (undeployed) response shape.

Fix: accept the legacy response shape (missing field = legacy success), fail only on an explicit negative receipt or when the capability has been negotiated, and add a regression test that uses the released provider's response shape.
